title: Fanout of a compiled circuit
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $c$ be a Boolean circuit tree on $n$ variables, and let $gs$ be a finite list of gates on natural-number-indexed vertices such that every input to its $i$th gate has index less than $n+i$. Compiling $c$ after $gs$ appends some list $ext$ of gates. Among the appended gates, each vertex of index at least $n$ is used as an input at most once; vertices corresponding to gates in $gs$ are not used, and the root vertex is not used when its index is at least $n$. The root index is either less than $n$ or at least $n+|gs|$. Every vertex whose index is at least $n+|gs|$ and less than $n+|gs|+|ext|$, except the root, is used exactly once as an input to the appended gates.
hypotheses_covered: $c$ is a Boolean circuit tree on $n$ variables
$gs$ is a finite list of gates
Each input index of the $i$th gate in $gs$ is less than $n+i
